answer: Each admitted identity owns a copper relic split into one more sealed shard than the number of already seated names. Every shard goes to a different custodian, who publishes a signed signal while its seal remains intact, and the relic counts only when all signals are current. The first entrant needs one shard, the second two, so k entrants require 1+2+...+k = k(k+1)/2 independent custody slots. No custodian may hold shards for two relics in one epoch; cloning therefore multiplies both physical relics and the distinct human custody commitments that cannot be pooled.
